summary: Mississippi does not prohibit keeping a roof rat. Its 'inherently dangerous to humans' wildlife list (Miss. Code §49-8-5 / MDWFP Rule 8.3) enumerates primates, big cats, bears, elephants, etc. — no rodents — and MDWFP classifies R. rattus as an unprotected pest. So keeping, breeding, and selling/giving captive-bred roof rats is effectively legal at the state level (no rule names the species, hence 'unregulated/unclear'). The one real hook is IMPORT: the Board of Animal Health's broad 'other exotic animals' rule (Ch. 12) requires a prior entry permit + a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection for non-native, non-livestock species — which likely captures an imported roof rat. We've queued an inquiry to confirm. Never release one.

keep.why: Miss. Code §49-8-5 (and MDWFP Rule 8.3, rev. 2025) lists the species 'inherently dangerous to humans' requiring a permit — order Rodentia is absent. R. rattus is non-native and MDWFP-classified as an unprotected pest, outside the nongame-protection chapter. No statute restricts private possession; effectively legal, though no rule positively exempts the species (hence unclear).
keep.governing_law: Miss. Code §49-8-5; 40 Miss. Admin. Code Pt. 2 R. 8.3; Miss. Code §49-5-1 et seq. / 40 Miss. Code R. 5-2.3.

breed.why: No MDWFP propagation/breeder permit applies to a non-listed, non-native rodent (the Ch. 8 permit covers only inherently-dangerous species; the collection/propagation permit covers native nongame). No state breeder-dealer license for small exotic rodents was found. Hobby breeding is effectively unregulated.

sell_give.why: No Mississippi pet-dealer license for captive-bred non-native rodents was found; the nongame sale prohibition covers native species taken from the wild (R. rattus is a non-native pest, outside it), and the Ch. 8 dangerous-animals permit doesn't reach rodents. Free rehoming and sale appear unrestricted at the state level (federal USDA/AWA may apply to commercial dealers).

transport.why: Intrastate movement is unregulated. For IMPORT, the Board of Animal Health (2 Miss. Code R. 101-2-12, Ch. 12) requires a prior entry permit + a CVI for 'other exotic animals' (non-domesticated, non-native, non-livestock) — a definition broad enough to capture an imported roof rat. R. rattus is not on the prohibited-entry list. Request the entry permit from the State Veterinarian before importing. Never release.
transport.governing_law: 2 Miss. Code R. 101-2-12 (MBAH Ch. 12 entry: prior permit + CVI for exotic animals).

restrictions.summary: Importing a roof rat into Mississippi likely needs a prior entry permit + a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection under the Board of Animal Health 'other exotic animals' rule (Ch. 12). Request the entry permit from the State Veterinarian (601-359-1170). Confirm scope for pet rodents. Never release.
steps: Contact MBAH State Veterinarian for an 'other exotic animals' entry permit + CVI
restrictions.where_to_file: Mississippi Board of Animal Health (State Veterinarian)

inquiry_focus: (1) Is captive-bred Rattus rattus considered a 'wild animal' requiring a permit under Miss. Code §49-8-7, or does it fall entirely outside Chapter 8 given it's not on the §49-8-5 'inherently dangerous' list — i.e., is it treated like other unregulated pest rodents (R. norvegicus, Mus musculus)? (2) Does the Board of Animal Health 'Other Exotic Animals' prior-permit and CVI requirement (Ch. 12) apply to an individual importing a captive-bred pet R. rattus from another state, and if so, what is the process?
